item.title: Cannabis operators with Toledo businesses targeted in state anti-trust lawsuit
item.description: COLUMBUS — The parent companies of Toledo’s cannabis businesses are among the nine multistate operators accused by Ohio Attorney General Dave Yost of engaging in anti-competitive conduct.

item.title: Local man gets 20 years for sexual contact with minors, child pornography
item.description: A 53-year-old Lucas County man has received a 20-year federal prison sentence after being convicted at two jury trials of pedophilia related charges.

item.title: Family files civil suit over son’s alleged abuse by Wood County Fair president
item.description: BOWLING GREEN — A Bradner, Ohio, family has sued the Wood County Fair civilly, alleging that it negligently allowed its former president to groom and sexually abuse a 17-year-old boy.

item.title: Portal pieces playing big roles for Bowling Green men’s basketball
item.description: BOWLING GREEN — In the current era of college basketball, rosters and seasons are continually shaped by transfers. The Bowling Green State University men’s basketball team is no exception, as five of the top seven team leaders in minutes per game joined the Falcons from other programs in the offseason.

item.title: Briggs: As Bowling Green hockey crowds soar, the madness — and magic — is back on Mercer Road
item.description: BOWLING GREEN — It is not just the magic of the old barn.

item.title: Sylvania schools unveils first responder program for high schoolers
item.description: Steve Urbanski, career readiness coordinator for Sylvania schools, shared with the school board a problem many fire departments would like to have: too many people applying for training.

item.title: MLB to produce local broadcasts for Tigers, Red Wings with fate of FanDuel Sports Network uncertain
item.description: DETROIT — The Detroit Tigers will have their local television broadcasts produced and distributed by Major League Baseball this season.

item.title: Oregon City Council kills 6-month extension on data center project
item.description: The Oregon City Council did not grant an extension to a developer to finalize plans for a $2 billion data center planned for the city.

item.title: Pistons snap Hornets' 9-game streak with 110-104 win in game marred by fight, ejections
item.description: CHARLOTTE, N.C. — Cade Cunningham had 33 points and nine rebounds, and the Detroit Pistons hung on to beat Charlotte 110-104 on Monday night, snapping the Hornets' nine-game winning streak in a wild game that included a fight and four player ejections.

item.title: Editorial: State on trial, too
item.description: Former FirstEnergy CEO Chuck Jones and Vice President Michael Dowling are on trial in Akron accused by the state of bribing former Public Utilities Commission of Ohio Chairman Sam Randazzo to use his regulatory position in aid of the company. The very nature of this case puts Ohio’s state government on trial as well.
